newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary APV to raise Antenna Hungaria's equity.
newsitem.headline: Hungary APV to raise Antenna Hungaria's equity.

text.p: The state privatisation agency APV has decided to raise the equity of Hungarian broadcasting company Antenna Hungaria Rt by 2.5 billion forints and is expected to approve a further two billion forints in January, the company said.

"The first 2.5 billion forints was approved on Thursday and the APV board will meet early in January to approve another two billion," Antenna Hungaria director Miklos Ditvai told Reuters in confirmation of an earlier announcement by government spokesman Elemer Kiss.
APV first proposed a 2.5 billion forint private capital increase for the company, which broadcasts all Hungary's radio and television programmes, in July, but it has been delayed several times.
At the time the company was owed 2.5 billion forints in unpaid broadcasting fees by Hungarian Radio and Hungarian Television.
Antenna is also responsible for preparing the country's broadcasting infrastructure for the privatisation of two national television channels and a number of radio stations later this year.
Antenna Hungaria invited tenders on Wednesday for the provision and installation of new equipment worth 4.5 billion forints. The deadline for submission of bids is December 23.
"The 2.5 billion forint raise will happen following its approval by a company general meeting at the end of January," Ditvai said.
